title: Flavor improvement of soy sauce driven by process optimization: analysis of key aroma compounds and molecular docking study
content:
Abstract

BACKGROUND

This study aimed to optimize the high-salt dilute-state fermentation process of soy sauce and to elucidate the key aroma compounds and their interactions with olfactory receptors.

RESULTS

The optimal conditions (soybean meal-to-roasted wheat ratio 6:4, salinity 200 g kg−1, staged temperature rise, co-inoculation with Tetragenococcus halophilus and Zygosaccharomyces rouxii GS2-3) yielded amino acid nitrogen and total nitrogen of 9.7 and 17.3 g L−1, respectively. A total of 110 volatile compounds were identified. Orthogonal partial least squares discriminant analysis, odor activity value calculation, aroma recombination and omission experiments revealed 4-Hydroxy-2(or 5)-ethyl-5(or 2)-methyl-3(2H)-furanone (HEMF) and phenylacetaldehyde as the key aroma compounds. Molecular docking confirmed their strong binding to olfactory receptors, with binding energies of −5.50 to −3.97 kcal mol−1 for HEMF and −5.21 to −4.14 kcal mol−1 for phenylacetaldehyde.

CONCLUSION

The optimized process significantly improved the physicochemical indices and volatile diversity of soy sauce. HEMF and phenylacetaldehyde were identified as pivotal aroma-active compounds with stable receptor binding. This study provides a theoretical basis for flavor enhancement in high-salt liquid-state soy sauce. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.
